items.title: Section: Taking the Precepts Alone Before an Image of the Buddha — The Full Self-Ordination Formula

items.zh: 又諸菩薩欲受菩薩淨戒律儀，若不會遇具足功德補特伽羅，爾時應對如來像前，自受菩薩淨戒律儀。應如是受，偏袒右肩，右膝著地，或蹲、跪、坐，作如是言：我如是名，仰啟十方一切如來、已入大地諸菩薩眾，我今欲於十方世界佛菩薩所，誓受一切菩薩學處，誓受一切菩薩淨戒。謂律儀戒、攝善法戒、饒益有情戒。如是學處、如是淨戒，過去一切菩薩已具，未來一切菩薩當具，普於十方現在一切菩薩今具。於是學處、於是淨戒，過去一切菩薩已學，未來一切菩薩當學，普於十方現在一切菩薩今學。第二、第三亦如是說，說已應起。所餘一切如前應知。
items.en: Furthermore, when a bodhisattva wishes to receive the bodhisattva precepts but cannot find a person possessing the genuine virtue needed to properly administer them, that bodhisattva should, at that time, receive the bodhisattva precepts entirely alone before an image of the Tathāgata. The precepts should be received in this way: baring the right shoulder, the right knee touching the ground, either crouching, kneeling, or seated, and speaking these words: "I, so-named, humbly address the buddhas of the ten directions and the assembly of bodhisattvas who have already entered the grounds. I now wish, before the buddhas and bodhisattvas of the worlds of the ten directions, to vow to undertake every bodhisattva learning, and to vow to receive every bodhisattva precept — namely, the precept of discipline, the precept of gathering wholesome dharmas, and the precept of benefiting sentient beings. These learnings, these precepts, every bodhisattva of the past has already fully possessed; every bodhisattva of the future will come to fully possess; and every bodhisattva presently existing throughout the ten directions fully possesses even now. In these learnings, in these precepts, every bodhisattva of the past has already trained; every bodhisattva of the future will come to train; and every bodhisattva presently existing throughout the ten directions is training even now." This should be said a second and a third time in the same way, and, once spoken, the bodhisattva should rise. Every other detail should be understood exactly as described earlier.

items.title: Section: Why Compassionate Exception Never Counts as "Irredeemable" Violation — and the Buddha's Own Teaching on Anger Versus Love

items.zh: 又於菩薩犯戒道中，無無餘犯。如世尊說：是諸菩薩多分應與瞋所起犯，非貪所起。當知此中所說密意。謂諸菩薩愛諸有情、憐諸有情增上力故，凡有所作一切皆是菩薩所作，非非所作；非作所作可得成犯。若諸菩薩憎諸有情、嫉諸有情，不能修行自他利行，作諸菩薩所不應作；作不應作可得成犯。又諸菩薩軟中上犯，如攝事分應當了知。
items.en: Furthermore, within what is, for bodhisattvas, a path of violation, there is no irredeemable violation. As the World-Honoured One taught: "For the most part, these bodhisattvas' violations arise from aversion, not from craving." One should understand the hidden intent taught here: precisely because bodhisattvas act under the powerful force of genuine love and compassion for beings, whatever they do in such cases is always what a bodhisattva ought to do, never what should not be done — and it is specifically failing to do what a bodhisattva ought to do that actually constitutes violation. But bodhisattvas who act from hatred and jealousy towards beings, unable to practise what genuinely benefits self and other, and who do what a bodhisattva ought never to do — it is this doing of what ought not be done that constitutes genuine violation. Furthermore, bodhisattva violations come in soft, middling, and severe grades, exactly as should be understood from the Compendium of Determinations.

items.title: Section: The Three Kinds of Completeness — and Their Three Shadows of Decline

items.zh: 如是菩薩依止一切自毘奈耶勤學所學，便得成就三種圓滿，安樂而住。一者、成就加行圓滿，二者、成就意樂圓滿，三者、成就宿因圓滿。云何名為加行圓滿？謂諸菩薩於淨戒中行無缺犯，於身語意清淨現行，不數毀犯發露自惡。如是名為加行圓滿。云何名為意樂圓滿？謂諸菩薩為法出家，不為活命；求大菩提，非為不求；為求沙門、為求涅槃，非為不求。如是求者，不住懈怠下劣精進，不雜眾多惡不善法、雜染後有、有諸熾然眾苦異熟、當來所有生老病死。如是名為意樂圓滿。云何名為宿因圓滿？謂諸菩薩，昔餘生中修福修善，故於今世種種衣服、飲食、臥具、病緣醫藥資身什物自無匱乏，復能於他廣行惠施。如是名為宿因圓滿。菩薩如是依毘奈耶勤學所學，成就如是三種圓滿，安樂而住。與此相違，當知成就三種衰損，危苦而住。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, relying on their own complete discipline, diligently train in what should be trained, come to accomplish three kinds of completeness, and dwell in genuine ease: first, accomplishing completeness of practice; second, accomplishing completeness of intention; third, accomplishing completeness of prior cause. What is completeness of practice? It is when bodhisattvas conduct themselves within the pure precepts without any lapse or violation, act with genuine purity in body, speech, and mind, do not repeatedly transgress, and, should they transgress, openly confess their own wrongdoing. This is called completeness of practice. What is completeness of intention? It is when bodhisattvas leave the household life for the sake of the dharma, not merely to make a living; genuinely seek supreme awakening, never failing to seek it; and genuinely seek the state of a true renunciant and genuine nirvana, never failing to seek them. Seeking in this way, they do not settle for lazy, inferior effort, do not mix in the many kinds of unwholesome conduct, do not accumulate defiled future existence, do not accumulate the ripening of intensely burning future suffering, and do not accumulate future birth, ageing, sickness, and death. This is called completeness of intention. What is completeness of prior cause? It is when bodhisattvas, having cultivated merit and goodness across former lifetimes, now in this present life lack nothing at all in clothing, food, bedding, medical care, and the other necessities of life, and are moreover able to extend generosity widely to others. This is called completeness of prior cause. Bodhisattvas who, relying on their discipline, diligently train in what should be trained in this way accomplish these three kinds of completeness, and dwell in genuine ease. In direct contrast, one should understand, failing to do so brings about three kinds of decline instead, and a life of genuine hardship.

items.title: Section: Fascicle 41 Closes — the Bodhisattva Precepts in Full, and a Bridge Towards the Difficult Practices Still to Come

items.zh: 如是略廣宣說菩薩若在家品、若出家品一切戒已。自斯已後，即於如是一切戒中，分出所餘難行戒等差別之相，應當了知。
items.en: Having now set out, in both brief and extensive detail, the complete precepts governing bodhisattvas of both the lay and the ordained orders, from this point onward, within this same entire body of precepts, a further set of distinguishing marks — the bodhisattva's difficult practices and the rest — will be drawn out and should be understood.

blocks.text: A short day to close fascicle 41 and the bodhisattva precepts.

"When a bodhisattva wishes to receive the precepts but cannot find a qualified person, they should go before an image of the Buddha" and take the precepts themselves, using the formula given: "I, so-and-so, report to all Buddhas and bodhisattvas of the ten directions: I now, before all of you, receive all the bodhisattva trainings and pure precepts…", three times. Master Cháng Bǎi describes the posture. This provision has made the bodhisattva precepts available to many practitioners without a teacher nearby.

"Within the bodhisattva's path there is no irredeemable violation." The Buddha said: "For the most part, bodhisattvas' violations arise from affection, not from anger": a bodhisattva errs more often by trying too hard to help than by hatred. Master Cháng Bǎi: "not doing what should be done: that is the violation."

Relying on complete discipline, one achieves: complete practice; complete intention; complete past causes. Their opposites are three kinds of decline. Venerable Miào Jìng: energy for merely contaminated merit is inferior diligence.

The lighter precepts are not a list of prohibitions so much as a portrait of attitudes: no pride, no grudges, no neglect of others or of study. Almost every offence turns on motive: "out of resentment" is tainted, "out of laziness" untainted, and genuine incapacity no offence at all. Fascicle 42 turns to the perfection of patience.

quiz.q: If no qualified person is available for confession, how does the treatise say the violation is cleared?
options: with pure intention, making a self-vow: "I will surely guard myself and never commit this again"
quiz.why: "The bodhisattva should … generate a genuinely pure resolve and make this solemn inner vow: 'I now resolve absolutely to guard myself going forward, and will never commit this offence again.'" Venerable Miào Jìng: this should be done before the Buddha, before an image; "vow" here means "resolve."

quiz.q: In self-ordination one says "I respectfully announce (qǐ) to all the Tathāgatas." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "qǐ"?
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "qǐ" carries the sense of reporting. Master Cháng Bǎi on the posture: a monastic bares the right shoulder and kneels on the right knee.

quiz.q: The English reads "it is specifically failing to do what a bodhisattva ought to do that actually constitutes violation." How do the two lectures read "fēi zuò suǒ zuò kě dé chéng fàn"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: "not doing what should be done is the violation" (as in the English); Miào Jìng: the two negatives make a positive — doing what a bodhisattva should do cannot become a violation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "not doing what should be done — that is the violation," matching the English. Venerable Miào Jìng: the two "not"s really amount to "is" — doing what should be done cannot become a violation. The two readings differ; the English follows Cháng Bǎi.

quiz.q: Training diligently by their own discipline, bodhisattvas accomplish which three completenesses?
options: completeness of practice, of intention, and of prior cause
quiz.why: "First, accomplishing completeness of practice; second, completeness of intention; third, completeness of prior cause." The opposite brings three kinds of decline. Venerable Miào Jìng: the discipline of the Lesser Vehicle is "another's discipline," in contrast to the bodhisattva's "own discipline."

quiz.q: Completeness of intention means not dwelling in "laziness or inferior diligence." How do the two lectures explain "inferior diligence"?
options: Miào Jìng: being energetic in contaminated merit-making; Cháng Bǎi: cultivating contaminated, affliction-linked, scattered merit — and, compared with the Great Vehicle, the two vehicles' diligence is also inferior
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: being full of energy for contaminated merit is inferior diligence. Master Cháng Bǎi: cultivating contaminated, affliction-linked, scattered merit is inferior diligence; and relative to the Great Vehicle, the two vehicles' diligence is inferior too.
